name: Custom OS
local_hint: Put any bootable .iso in the images folder and this box will boot the first one it finds. To name a specific image, or to give it UEFI, a different disk size or a provisioning script, drop a small .json in the os folder beside it and bind a box to it with /give @s virtualcomputers:custom_os[virtualcomputers:image_id="your_id"].
notes: The escape hatch, and deliberately not a separate feature - it is the third row of the plan's table, which is what makes Windows need no special case either. A custom box with nothing bound to it boots whatever ISO is in the images folder, which is exactly what phase 2 did, so nothing that already worked stopped working. A custom box bound to an entry id is that entry, including a recipe: an entry naming a base image and a provisioning script costs nothing to host and is what rescues architectures the appliance projects publish no image for.
